meta-desc: Handy tools by Populus Hu: live Markdown preview and Mermaid diagram rendering. Everything runs locally in your browser — no data is uploaded.
meta-desc-md: A Markdown live-preview tool running entirely in your browser, with code highlighting, tables and task lists.
meta-desc-mmd: A Mermaid diagram renderer running entirely in your browser — flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts and more, with SVG / PNG export.

hero-desc: Three tools that run entirely inside your browser. Your text and diagrams are never uploaded anywhere, and they keep working offline — every dependency is hosted right here, with no external CDN.
tools-desc: All three are pure front-end tools. Open and use — no sign-up needed.
card-md-desc: Write on the left, preview on the right, updated live. Tables, task lists and code highlighting are supported; drag in a .md file or export the result as HTML.
card-mmd-desc: Draw flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts and class diagrams from plain text. Live preview with error hints, and export to SVG or PNG.
note-local: These tools are pure front-end: all processing happens locally in your browser. The only network request is loading the page itself — save it, and it still opens offline.

meta-desc-bf: A Brainfuck editor and optimizing interpreter that runs entirely in your browser, with a peephole optimizer and a side-by-side interpreted vs JIT-compiled comparison.
bf-desc: Write code on the left, see output on the right. The built-in optimizer folds common idioms into single instructions, then runs the same IR through both an interpreter and a JIT.
bf-stdin-ph: Each , takes the next character; 0 once exhausted
bf-placeholder:
Write Brainfuck here…
Only + - < > [ ] . , are commands; every other character is ignored as a comment.
bf-err-ptr: Pointer out of range: the program walked outside the %s-cell tape
bf-err-steps: Step limit exceeded (probably an infinite loop)
bf-err-nocsp: new Function is blocked here (CSP), so the JIT is unavailable — fell back to the interpreter
bf-toast-truncated: Output too long — showing the first 20,000 characters only
bf-note: The optimizer is a pure source-to-source rewrite: [-] becomes a clear, [->+<] becomes a single transfer, [>] becomes a scan, and overwritten stores are dropped. Both timings run the same optimized IR — the only difference is that one is interpreted while the other is compiled into real nested JS while-loops.
card-bf-desc: A minimal language with just 8 commands. The built-in optimizer folds common idioms into single instructions, then runs the same IR through an interpreter and a JIT to compare timings.
